definitions.explanation: A person who works at a bank. The term covers all bank staff from tellers to office workers, but does not include executive management.

examples.japanese: {行員|こういん}に{口座|こうざ}の{開設|かいせつ}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I asked a bank employee to open an account.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{大手|おおて}{銀行|ぎんこう}の{行員|こういん}として{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: She works as an employee at a major bank.

examples.japanese: {窓口|まどぐち}の{行員|こういん}が{丁寧|ていねい}に{手続|てつづ}きの{説明|せつめい}をしてくれた。
examples.english: The bank clerk at the counter politely explained the procedure to me.

notes:
A compound of {行|こう} (abbreviation of {銀行|ぎんこう}, bank) and {員|いん} (member, staff). This word follows the common Japanese pattern of abbreviating an organization name and adding {員|いん} to refer to its employees, similar to {社員|しゃいん} (company employee) and {駅員|えきいん} (station staff).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {銀行|ぎんこう}{行員|こういん}: bank employee (with full form for clarity)
- {窓口|まどぐち}の{行員|こういん}: teller, counter clerk
- {行員|こういん}として{勤|つと}める: to work as a bank employee

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {銀行員|ぎんこういん}: bank employee — the full, unabbreviated form; slightly more common in everyday speech
- {社員|しゃいん}: company employee — the parallel term for general companies
- {局員|きょくいん}: post office employee — the equivalent for postal workers
- {工員|こういん}: factory worker — a homophone with completely different meaning; uses {工|こう} (craft, factory) instead of {行|こう} (bank)
